cells.tense: You're in the middle of it with both hands, and you're deciding as you go — nothing here is running on habit.
cells.ask: Let one person hear what the tending cost you — say it plain once the work is done, and let the finishing be enough.
cells.core:
You're the one who sets the portions here, and you do it awake. When two needs pull at you at the same time, you hold both instead of letting one go short — not by force, just steady attention. Around you, people get their share because the scale stays honest, and you feel the balance the same way you'd feel a table that's level under your hands.

The weight of holding that is real, and mostly it goes unseen. You know exactly what you've put in, and it hasn't been said back to you. Naming it out loud once isn't asking for a medal. It's letting the account close, so the next round can start clean.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the scale honest, and you know what you spent to do it.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with your own hands, on purpose
cells.place: where what each person puts in and gets back gets weighed and set right

cells.tense: You're standing in a future that hasn't happened yet, bracing for it like it's already here.
cells.ask: Finish one thing before you start the next — let it be actually done, and let the satisfaction of that be the whole reward for a day.
cells.core:
You're providing for moments that haven't arrived. Before anyone asks, you've already worked out what they'll need and how you'll supply it, and the scale has tipped, because you're weighing yourself against a future nobody has written yet. The care is running ahead of the thing it's for.

This same care, when it's steady, is just you tending what's in front of you at the pace it actually grows — two things held at once, neither one starved, your attention on the ground under your feet. Nothing has to be solved in advance. Let one thing run all the way to its end, and stand in what's already here instead of what's next.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed behind you, waiting for it to open again.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been tending and keep going with it, even a little, today — let that be the hoping.
cells.core:
Somewhere along the way the ledger stopped being kept. You stopped putting in, or stopped counting what you put in, and things around you have gone lopsided without anyone naming it. The care is still there. The hand that reaches for it isn't.

On a good day this is easy and unremarkable — you water what's in front of you, it grows, and you get to watch it grow. That's still within reach, and it doesn't take much to start. One small thing, kept at, and the balance begins coming back on its own. Persistence is what has kept things alive around you before, and it's the same hand you haven't lifted yet.
cells.sheetLine: The ledger stopped being kept and things went lopsided.

cells.tense: Your hand is already on the scale, and you'd tell anyone it's just the situation working itself out.
cells.ask: Say out loud that one thing you keep tending is yours to tend — and let what you've already given get its due.
cells.core:
You're the one setting what gets cared for around you — the small choices, what gets time, what gets left — and you do it without calling it a decision. Look at what runs well near you. That's you holding the balance, and you'd credit the schedule or the season long before you'd credit yourself.

When it's going well, you know what you've put in and you don't mind saying so. That hasn't stopped being true. You just stopped saying it. Your intent has been plain to everyone but you this whole time — and underneath it there's a simpler thing, which is that you get to put the pen down when the work is done.
